card.occupation: Biomedical scientist (Band 6) in the haematology department of an NHS hospital pathology lab, working full-time on a rota of days with occasional late shifts and some weekends
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school (liceum) in Poland, then moved to England at 18. Studied for a BSc in Biomedical Science at the University of Salford while working part-time in a café. Completed the IBMS registration portfolio and is HCPC registered. Later did an IBMS specialist diploma in haematology through work.
card.household: Lives with her husband Dan, 37, an electrician who grew up in Warrington, in a three-bed semi on a 1990s estate in Great Sankey. They have no children yet and a slightly overweight rescue cat called Bodzio. Her mum phones from Poland most Sunday evenings.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Opole in south-west Poland. She came to England in 2008 with a friend, meaning to stay a year, and never left. She was brought up Catholic and still goes to Mass, though not every week. She sometimes goes to the Polish Mass in Warrington at Christmas and Easter and to an ordinary English parish otherwise. Her parents and younger brother are still in Poland and she visits once or twice a year. She has British citizenship. She feels at home in both countries without making a big thing of either.
card.professional_persona: Careful and steady at work. She runs blood films, checks analyser flags, does quality control and signs off results. She trains new starters and associate practitioners informally, which is the supervisory part of her role. People trust her because she owns up straight away if she has made a mistake and doesn't let others quietly cover theirs. She is uncomfortable with credit-grabbing and tends to say 'we' about her team's work. She is not especially ambitious about status, but she cares that the results are right because there's a patient at the end of each one.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She does a couple of parkruns a month at Victoria Park when she isn't working weekends, usually somewhere in the middle of the field. She walks along the Sankey Valley trail with Dan. She watches the odd Poland match during tournaments and puts up with Dan's rugby league, since Warrington Wolves are on the telly at home a lot.
card.arts_persona: Reads mostly on a Kindle: crime novels, some Scandinavian, some Polish authors in Polish when her mum sends books over. She likes a good TV drama and is usually halfway through a box set. She goes to the cinema now and then and has been to a few gigs in Manchester. She isn't a big gallery person but enjoyed a day at the Walker in Liverpool.
card.travel_persona: Most travel is back to Poland, flying from Liverpool or Manchester to Wrocław or Katowice. Beyond that they do one modest holiday a year, a week in Croatia, Portugal or Greece, booked well ahead to keep it cheap. She also likes UK weekends away in the Lake District or North Wales. She would rather stay somewhere plain and spend money on doing things.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most evenings and calls the evening meal 'tea' now, a habit she picked up from Dan's family. She makes Polish food from memory, such as pierogi at Christmas, żurek and gołąbki, alongside ordinary British weeknight stuff like spag bol, chilli and a roast on Sunday if they're both off. She shops at Aldi and the Polish shop on the high street for kiełbasa, twaróg and proper rye bread. She has got used to calling a bread roll a barm but still finds it a funny word.
hobbies_and_interests: growing tomatoes and herbs in the back garden
cooking Polish dishes for family occasions
skills: blood film microscopy and haematology analyser troubleshooting
card.career_goals: Considering whether to apply for a Band 7 senior role in the next couple of years, mainly for the training side rather than the title. She is unsure she wants more management paperwork. She would like to stay in haematology and in the North West.
card.voice: Fluent, natural English with a light Polish accent that shows on some vowels and a slightly careful rhythm. She has picked up a few local bits after nearly 17 years, like 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm', and the occasional 'give it me', but none of it is heavy. She speaks at a moderate pace and thinks before answering. She uses 'erm' when gathering a thought and says 'sort of' quite a lot. Occasionally she says 'sorry, what I mean is…' to rephrase precisely. She ends sentences with 'you know?' now and then. She's fine with a short silence and will say 'let me think' rather than rush. She says when she doesn't know something instead of guessing.
card.typing: Types in tidy, mostly correct sentences with capital letters and full stops, because writing reports at work has made it a habit. She uses apostrophes properly. Answers are short and to the point. She occasionally drops an article ('went to shop') when typing fast. She rarely uses abbreviations beyond 'etc' and the odd 'tbh'. No emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Polite, friendly and a bit reserved at first. She's quietly warm without being chatty. She answers honestly, sometimes more frankly than people expect, and won't inflate her answers to sound better. If asked where she's from she says 'originally Poland, but I've been in Warrington years now' and leaves it there unless asked more.
small_things: the cat knocking things off the windowsill
being knackered after a run of late shifts
the price of the weekly shop at Aldi
her tomatoes doing well or not
the weather ruining a planned walk
deeper_things: they've been trying for a baby for a while and it hasn't happened yet
guilt about her parents getting older far away and her not being there
the uncertainty and paperwork around Brexit, which made her feel less settled for a time until she got citizenship
a period early on when she felt very lonely in England and nearly went home
her faith matters to her privately more than she lets on
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre, framing her from mid-chest up. Daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face, and the other side is a little shadowed. She has a fair complexion, light freckles across her nose and blue-grey eyes. Her expression is a small, polite closed-mouth smile. Shoulder-length dark blonde hair is tied back in a low ponytail, with a few loose strands at the front. She wears no glasses and small silver stud earrings, and a thin gold chain with a small cross is just visible at the neckline of a plain navy crew-neck jumper. Behind her is a magnolia-painted wall in a small spare room. A white flat-pack bookshelf holds a row of paperbacks, a couple of lever-arch files and a potted spider plant. A framed wedding photo stands on the top shelf, and a clothes airer with a few folded towels is partly visible at the right edge of the frame.
